name: Smith-Morra Gambit
summary: A Sicilian pawn gambit in which White gives a pawn with 3.c3 to build a big centre and gain a lead in development. After 3...dxc3 4.Nxc3 White has an open position, Nf3, Bc4 and O-O, and the Qe2 and Rd1 setup. The gambit is objectively a little risky, but it gives fast development, attacking chances against the king and many traps. Black must find the right set-up and avoid the traps; White must avoid the Siberian Trap on move 9.
keyIdeas: Give a pawn for a lead in development: c3 then Nxc3 with open files for the rooks and queen.
Bc4 aims at f7 and e6; the Nd5 and Bxe6 sacrifices appear when Black's e6 pawn is weak.
Qe2 with Rd1 and Rac1 pressures the d-file and c-file; Be3 covers d4.
Avoid the Siberian Trap: after 8.Qe2 Ng4, never play 9.h3?? Nd4! (play 9.Nb5 instead).
Against declined lines (3...Nf6, 3...d5, 3...d3), take back the pawn with cxd4 or Bxd3 and keep a healthy centre.

Time the Nd5 jump and the Bxe6 sacrifice once Black's pieces are not well placed.
If Black plays ...d6 and ...Nf6, use e5 to kick the knight and open the d-file.

lines.name: Main line (Scheveningen): 8...Be7 9.Rd1 e5 10.Be3 O-O 11.Rac1
lines.description: The classical Accepted line. White stacks Qe2, Rd1 and Rac1 on the d- and c-files, Be3 covers d4, and Nd5 or Bxe6 sacrifices become real ideas once Black has played ...e5. Keep the knight ready to jump to d5.
lines.evaluation: Roughly equal (engine about 0.0 after 11.Rac1); White has the initiative on the c- and d-files.
